One of the player position battles I've discussed more than anyone else this offseason has been Bhayshul Tuten vs. Chris Rodriguez 

- Here is all of the data and analysis I've done on both RBs this offseason

[Bhayshul Tuten]

1. Might get the majority of the receiving work out of the backfield. How fantasy-lucrative is that, though?

- The Jaguars ranked 23rd in XFP/G to RBs last season (6.5), and a healthy LeQuint Allen could hurt this "upside" case even further 

- Tuten's 1.05 YPRR ranked 30th among all RBs in 2025 as well 

2. If Tuten was so "explosive" in college, why didn't that translate to the NFL at all?

- His 6.7% Explosive Run Rate ranked 50th among all RBs, compared to Rodriguez's 14.3% (RB8) 

3. But, but, but... Tuten was only a short-yardage back; that's why! 

- He had 21 rush attempts with 3 or fewer yards to go (25.3% of his attempts) vs. Rodriguez's 26 (23.2%), so that argument falls flat 

- Even if we look at rush attempts where Tuten had at least 3.0 YBCO/Att, he still ranked 46th in Explosive Run Rate (23.8%) vs. Rodriguez who ranked 3rd (44.4%)

4. What from his rookie season gives us any inclination that Tuten is a breakout candidate in 2026?

- He had 8 games with 3.5 YPC or less, and only 2 games where he recorded more than a single reception

5. The entire argument for Tuten hinges on his college production, which led to him being only a 4th-round draft pick, and the increased opportunities with Travis Etienne gone 

- Rookie rushing efficiency doesn't matter much, but Tuten was rather unimpressive in Year 1

6. After watching every touch Tuten had last season, there was nothing he flashed on tape that impressed me much at all 

- The majority of his TDs were essentially "walk-ins" as well 

[Chris Rodriguez]

1. Every RB scatterplot chart I've made this offseason has shown Rodriguez ranked as a top-tier rusher 

- Rush EPA/A vs. Success Rate, FPOE vs. RYOE/Att, while ranking top-10 in "Cool Shit" percentage 

2. Rodriguez has ranked as one of the most efficient goal-line backs in the league over the last two seasons 

- 1.63 YPC (RB1), 50.0% Success Rate (RB4), 13.4 RYOE (RB1), and 0.481 EPA/A (RB1) 

3. Over his 3-year NFL career, Rodriguez has been one of the most efficient rushers in the league 

- Top-10 in explosive rush rate all 3 seasons, MTF/Att, and YACO/Att

4. In 2025 alone, Rodriguez was more efficient that Tuten across the board 

- YPC, Explosive Run Rate, Success Rate, and YACO/Att

5. Rodriguez has familiarity playing with Liam Coen and is a great fit for the rushing style Coen has vocalized desiring in 2026 

- His 2025 tape looked better than Tuten's and he's been listed as a co-starter on the Week 1 depth chart 

6. Even though he has little to no pass-catching upside, I think Rodriguez is 100% worth rostering right now

- Pick him up off your waivers if he's just sitting there

Let’s talk about building a “league-winning” roster.

Most of the discussion around this topic centers around chasing “UPSIDE.”

While I agree with this core principle – the principle is often used to hijack the entire conversation – to the point where players who “only beat their ADP by a few spots” are actually viewed as “bad” picks.

Essentially – if a player isn’t a “league-winning” pick, they’re a “bad” pick.

This notion is used to dismiss “boring” but productive veterans – all the time.

I’d like to challenge this notion of them being “bad” picks – as it simply is not supported by the data.

Via @RyanJ_Heath’s “Anatomy of a League-Winner” series…

We know that:

There were 18 “league-winning” players in 2024.

There were 18 “league-winning” players in 2025.

Essentially – we get 18 “league-winning” players per season.

(“League-winner” being defined as a player to make 55%+ of playoff rosters, using leagues where 4 out of 10 leagues make playoffs as the baseline)

Out of the 18 "league-winners" in 2025 – 13/18 (72.2%) were drafted within the first 5 rounds.

Out of the 18 “league-winners” in 2024 – 17/18 (94.4%) were drafted inside the first 6 rounds; all of the QB's/RB's/WR's (15/15) inside the first 5 rounds.

In total – 30/36 “league-winners” (83.3%) over the last 2 seasons have been drafted inside the first 6 rounds.

Essentially – you only need “league-winners” with your first 5-6 picks.

& your goal with your remaining 8-10 picks should quite literally be:

“To draft players who slightly outperform their ADP’s – while avoiding players who slightly underperform them.”

This does not apply to the QB position – where you still have a 10%+ chance historically at drafting a league-winner in RD9-12; this is the one position you should still be targeting “league-winners” outside of RD1-5.

Otherwise – you simply want to beat ADP in RD6-12.

Once you get to your last 2-3 picks – you can shift back towards prioritizing only “UPSIDE” – as floor is nonexistent that late.

Your mindset should shift & evolve throughout the draft.

Instead of simply “swinging for a league-winner” at every available pick, I believe the optimal strategy is to:

📌 Target “league-winners” RD1-5
📌 Beat ADP RD6-12 (outside of QB)
📌 Target “league-winners” RD13+

Not exclusively – but as a general guideline.

Your scope should widen from targeting league-winners early, to also including ADP-beaters in the middle rounds, back towards prioritizing upside-only with your last few picks.

Your strategy should shift based on the portion of the draft you’re in.

THAT’s how you craft a true “league-winning” roster.
